summary.oneLiner: Stallion is transitioning from a blender/distributor to an integrated manufacturer with a 10k MT R-32 plant (Aug '26) and expanded helium infrastructure, targeting a PAT margin jump from 10% to 24%. While FY26 guidance (INR 430cr Rev, INR 40cr PAT) remains intact, execution risks on capex funding (Rights Issue) and plant commissioning delays (Khalapur/Mambatu to Mar-Apr '26) are key near-term monitors.

one-line thesis: Stallion is transitioning from a blender/distributor to an integrated manufacturer with a 10k MT R-32 plant (Aug '26) and expanded helium infrastructure, targeting a PAT margin jump from 10% to 24%. While FY26 guidance (INR 430cr Rev, INR 40cr PAT) remains intact, execution risks on capex funding (Rights Issue) and plant commissioning delays (Khalapur/Mambatu to Mar-Apr '26) are key near-term monitors.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 104.87cr (Q3, +23.2% YoY), INR 321.18cr (9M, +41.7% YoY); EBITDA: INR 13.56cr (Q3), INR 43.69cr (9M, +48.6% YoY); PAT: INR 11.12cr (Q3), INR 32.9cr (9M, +72.8% YoY); Order Book: Not disclosed (Spot/Contract mix); Net Debt: Debt-free (Promoter injected interest-free loan for R-32 kickstart); One-offs: Promoter sold 2% stake to fund interest-free loan for R-32 plant due to failed preferential issue.
guidance: FY26 Revenue: INR 430cr; FY26 PAT: INR 40cr; Margin Target: 24% PAT (up from current ~10%) driven by new products; CAGR Target: 30-35% over next 3 years.
order book & pipeline: Not explicitly quantified; Management cites 200+ customers across 15 countries; R-32 plant expected to contribute INR 275cr revenue in first 6 months (Oct '26-Mar '27).
segment / subsidiary detail: Refrigerants: R-32 backward integration (10k MT Bhilwara); Specialty Gases: Helium liquefaction/recovery (Khalapur & Mambatu), HFO blending; High-Purity: Semiconductor/Defense applications via SYS Advanced tie-up.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) R-32 captive production (10k MT) replacing imports; 2) Helium network expansion (West/South India) targeting INR 200cr revenue in 5 years; 3) Future HFO plant post-R-32 commissioning; 4) By-product commercialization.
margins & cost dynamics: Current PAT margin ~10%; Target PAT margin 24% for new products (R-32, Helium); Cost competitiveness via backward integration and economies of scale (doubled R-32 capacity from 5k to 10k MT).
capex / expansion: R-32 Plant (Bhilwara): INR 364cr (funded via Rights Issue); Helium upgrades (Khalapur/Mambatu): INR 15-20cr (internal accruals); Land (Bhilwara): INR 12cr (subsidized).
capital allocation: Rights Issue of INR 364cr planned for R-32 plant; Promoter to subscribe proportionately (including conversion of interest-free loan); No further equity dilution expected post-rights; Debt-free stance maintained.
risks & watch-items: 1) Commissioning delays (Khalapur helium delayed 3 months due to pressure upgrade to 300 bar; Mambatu re-engineered for larger scale); 2) Execution risk on rapid capex deployment; 3) Raw material volatility (imported helium/components); 4) Regulatory changes in fluorocarbons.
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term structural shift to manufacturing; Defensive on communication gaps regarding delays (cites 're-engineering' for better economics); Aggressive on margin expansion and market share capture.
non-obvious takeaways: Promoter's 2% stake sale was a bridge to fund R-32 kickstart after market volatility killed a preferential issue; R-32 capacity doubled mid-stream (5k to 10k MT) to avoid future shutdowns for expansion, signaling a 'big bang' manufacturing entry rather than phased learning.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

themes.title: Industrial gases, chlor-alkali & commodity chemicals
themes.need: A capacity-led commodity-chemical and industrial-gas cycle underpins the basic-materials chain - ELLEN on air-separation/industrial gases; EPIGRAL/CHEMPLASTS/DCW/DCMSHRIRAM/GHCL/TATACHEM/GNFC on chlor-alkali, soda-ash and vinyls; LORDSCHLO on caustic; CHEMBONDCH on water-treatment chemicals. Pricing/utilization and energy costs are the near-term swing factors.
themes.driver: Caustic/soda-ash price recovery; utilization ramp on new capacity; energy-cost relief.
